column1: To make this comparison for a real economy, such as the U.S. economy, we need an estimate of the growth rate of output (n + g) and an estimate of the net marginal product of capital (MPK - δ). Real GDP in the United States grows an average of 3 percent per year, so n + g = 0.03. We can estimate the net marginal product of capital from the following three facts: 1. The capital stock is about 2.5 times one year’s GDP. 2. Depreciation of capital is about 10 percent of GDP. 3. Capital income is about 30 percent of GDP.
